title: [Open to all] Share a tip about a scam you've seen recently

done: One new line in [`awareness/tips.md`](https://github.com/CyberSecTober/Cybersectober/blob/main/awareness/tips.md) in the usual format: `- **Short tip title**, one sentence explaining it. (@your-github-username)`. No real names, phone numbers or links to the scam.

title: [Open to all] Build a small defensive security tool
track: Any track (put it in the folder that fits: awareness, api-security, ai-security or community)
what: Already built a security script or tool, or want to? Share a small tool that helps people defend themselves. Ideas: a password strength checker, a security headers checker for your own website, a phishing URL analyser that works offline, a log parser that flags failed logins, a secrets scanner for your own repo, or a file integrity checker.
done:
- A new folder `<track>/tools/your-github-username-tool-name/` with your code and a `README.md` based on [`templates/tool.md`](https://github.com/CyberSecTober/Cybersectober/blob/main/templates/tool.md), including the YAML header, installation, usage and example output.
- It runs locally with clear instructions, and only touches systems and files the user owns.
- No binaries, archives, minified code or downloads from unknown URLs. No exploit code against real products.
- Your own original work, released under the repository's MIT licence.

title: [Open to all] Turn your security blog post into a guide
track: Any track (put it in the folder that fits)
what: Written a security blog post on Medium, Hashnode, Dev.to, LinkedIn or your own site? Bring it into the library so it stays free and easy to find. Rewrite it as a guide that stands on its own, and link your original post as the source.
done:
- A new file `<track>/your-github-username-topic.md` based on [`templates/guide.md`](https://github.com/CyberSecTober/Cybersectober/blob/main/templates/guide.md), with the YAML header.
- The full guide is in the file itself, not just a link or a summary. Add your original post under a "Source" heading at the end.
- The post must be your own. Defensive focus: explain what went wrong and how to prevent it, without step-by-step attack instructions.
- Any vulnerability you describe in a real product must already be reported and fixed.

title: [Open to all] Write a security checklist for a real situation
track: Any track (put it in the folder that fits)
what: Write a practical checklist someone can follow step by step. Ideas: setting up a new laptop or phone, securing a small business, before launching a website or API, travelling with devices, protecting a church, mosque or community group's accounts, or offboarding an employee.
done:
- A new file `<track>/your-github-username-checklist-topic.md` based on [`templates/checklist.md`](https://github.com/CyberSecTober/Cybersectober/blob/main/templates/checklist.md), with the YAML header.
- At least 10 clear, actionable items, grouped into sections, each with one line on why it matters.
- Says who the checklist is for.

title: [Open to all] Write a step-by-step security walkthrough
track: Any track (put it in the folder that fits)
what: Show people how to do one security task from start to finish, with screenshots or commands. Ideas: securing a GitHub account, setting up a password manager for your family, turning on full-disk encryption, inspecting your own network traffic with Wireshark, scanning your own website with OWASP ZAP, or setting up a firewall on a home router.
done:

- Numbered steps a beginner can follow, with the expected result after each step, and screenshots or commands where they help.
- Any scanning or testing is only done on systems you own or on deliberately vulnerable practice targets.

title: [Open to all] Explain an OWASP API Security Top 10 risk

- A vulnerable and a fixed code example for a fictional API using `example.com`.
- At least 3 prevention steps and how to test for the issue in your own API.
